title: standardize-rate-limit-idempotency-retry-after-streaming-tool-calls-openai-compat
author: Sofia Patel
description: Motivation: Inconsistent rate-limit semantics and idempotency handling across the API surface (hosted API, OpenAI-compat layer, streaming, and tool/function-calling) have caused client retries to behave non-deterministically and produced unnecessary retries/incidents. This PR unifies Retry-After handling, idempotency key semantics, and error codes across endpoints; fixes streaming disconnect semantics for partial tool responses; and updates the OpenAI-compat layer to mirror expected response shapes for 429 and idempotency-related errors. Changes include: - standardized Retry-After precedence: explicit Retry-After header (seconds) takes precedence; when present we also include x-retry-after-ms for millisecond precision for clients that prefer it; when Retry-After is missing but we have backend throttle windows we surface a Retry-After with the calculated seconds. - idempotency keys: introduce a unified middleware (idempotency.go) that canonicalizes X-Idempotency-Key (case-insensitive), normalizes whitespace, respects forwarded requests (preserves key across internal redirects) and stores receipts in the idempotency store with configurable TTL. The middleware emits metrics (idempotency.hit/miss/conflict) and exposes a small API for inspection (for SRE use). - consistent error codes: map internal throttle errors to 429 for client-rate-limits and 503 for backend overload; include machine-readable error codes in the JSON body (error.code = "rate_limit" | "backend_overload" | "idempotency_conflict"). The OpenAI-compat layer now returns payloads that match OpenAI semantics for 429 including 'type' and 'param' fields when applicable. - streaming stability: when a streaming connection drops during a tool/function call, the runtime now emits a final chunk indicating stream-terminated with boundary metadata and persists the partial tool result (if any) tied to the idempotency receipt so clients can retry safely and reclaim partial output via a /stream-recover endpoint. This prevents duplicate tool-execution when clients retry. - tool/function-calling semantics: tool calls that are side-effectful now require explicit idempotency keys; the runtime checks idempotency store prior to executing tool adapters to avoid duplicate external side effects. Tool adapter contract extended with an optional 'idempotency_context' field so adapters can perform safe dedupe where applicable. - OpenAI-compat updates: compatibility shim adjusted to surface the same Retry-After and idempotency headers that official OpenAI responses return; SDKs (python/ts) updated to prefer Retry-After and fallback to x-retry-after-ms. - docs and changelog: updated API reference and migration guide; included sample server and client behavior for streaming recovery and idempotency usage. Testing: unit tests for middleware, integration tests covering streaming disconnect + retry, a smoke test against a staging tool adapter that simulates side effects, and updated SDK unit tests. Backwards compatibility: default behavior is unchanged for clients that do not set X-Idempotency-Key; new behavior is opt-in via headers. Rollout plan: staged rollout behind feature flag; monitoring dashboards added (rate-limit-events, idempotency-conflicts, stream-recoveries). Checklist: - [x] Middleware implementation and unit tests - [x] Streaming termination + recovery path implemented - [x] OpenAI-compat response shape aligned - [x] SDKs updated (python/ts) - [x] Docs + migration guide updated - [x] SLO/alerting dashboard added - [x] Feature-flagged staged rollout (canary -> region -> all) Related work: ENG-4021 (idempotency store + metrics), ENG-4120 (streaming reliability), SUP-2104 (customer incident caused by mismatched 429 semantics).

review_comments: Ethan Miller: Can you explain why we choose Retry-After seconds as the canonical header vs x-retry-after-ms? Some clients expect millisecond precision.

Sofia Patel: We keep Retry-After (seconds) as the canonical HTTP header to match existing conventions and intermediaries. x-retry-after-ms is added as a companion header for millisecond precision for clients that need it; SDKs prefer Retry-After and fall back to x-retry-after-ms when available.
Priya Singh: The idempotency store TTL default looks short for some long-running tool calls. Can we make TTL configurable per-route?
Sofia Patel: Yes, TTL is configurable at the route level and we added a default of 24h; updated the middleware docs to show route-level overrides.
Liam O'Connor: Integration tests flaked once on CI (streaming disconnect). Was that the original issue?
Sofia Patel: CI flake was due to our test harness not waiting for background persistence; added a wait/retry and test now stable. Also added metrics to detect persistence latency.
Ethan Miller: We should ensure OpenAI-compat changes do not break customers parsing error shapes. Added a suggestion to include a compatibility flag.
Sofia Patel: Added feature flag and compatibility mode in openai-compat shim; default enabled for new responses but can be toggled per-tenant during rollout.
ci_details: CI summary: lint: pass; unit: pass; integration: pass (1 rerun for flake fixed); e2e: pass; security-scan: pass; deploy-preview: success. Flaky integration test was addressed by adding a wait loop and a metric assertion. All checks green before merge.
release_notes: Standardized rate-limit and idempotency semantics across API surfaces: consistent Retry-After/x-retry-after-ms headers, canonicalized X-Idempotency-Key handling, streaming recovery to avoid duplicate tool executions, and OpenAI-compat response alignment. Backwards compatible; opt-in behavior via headers and feature flags. See docs/reference/retry-after-idempotency.md for migration steps.
